item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 162318
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Sun Aug 16 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located west of Honolulu, Hawaii.

Western Portion of the East Pacific:
A broad area of low pressure could form well to the southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands during the middle to latter part of the week.
Environmental conditions appear conducive for gradual development of
this system, and a tropical depression could form towards the end of
the week and into the weekend, while the system moves generally
westward across the western portion of the east Pacific and into the
central Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams/Pasch
NNNN

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Public Advisory Number 18a
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM HST Sun Aug 16 2026 
000
WTPA32 PHFO 162354
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Intermediate Advisory Number 18A
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Sun Aug 16 2026
 
...LALA CONTINUES WESTWARD TO THE SOUTHWEST OF KAUAI COUNTY...
...OUTER BANDS OF LALA BRINGING HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS TO
PORTIONS OF THE SMALLER MAIN HAWAIIAN ISLANDS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM HST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.8N 160.9W
ABOUT 330 MI...530 KM WNW OF KAILUA-KONA HAWAII
ABOUT 195 MI...315 KM W OF HONOLULU HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 265 DEGREES AT 20 MPH...31 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

The Tropical Storm Warnings for Maui County, including the islands
of Maui, Lanai, Molokai and Kahoolawe, and for Oahu have been
discontinued.

SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:

A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Kauai County, including the islands of Kauai and Niihau

A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within the
next 12 hours.

Interests in the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument should
monitor the progress of Lala.

For storm information specific to your area, including possible
inland watches and warnings, please monitor products issued by your
local National Weather Service forecast office.
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM HST (0000 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 20.8 North, longitude 160.9 West. Lala is 
moving toward the west near 20 mph (31 km/h). A westward motion is 
forecast through Tuesday night, followed by a turn toward the 
west-northwest on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Little intensity change is expected through Monday. Some 
restrengthening is forecast thereafter, and Lala could become a 
hurricane again on Tuesday or Wednesday.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km)
from the center. A wind gust of 39 mph (63 km/h) was recently 
reported at Lihue Airport.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Lala can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP2 and WMO header WTPA42 PHFO.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions, especially in gusts, are ongoing 
across portions of Kauai County, with the strongest winds occurring 
in areas of higher terrain. Wind speeds atop mountains and on the 
windward and leeward slopes are often up to 30 percent stronger than 
the near-surface winds indicated in this advisory, and in some 
elevated locations could be even greater.
 
RAINFALL: Outer bands from Lala are expected to produce additional 
rainfall of 1 to 2 inches across windward portions of the Big Island 
and windward Maui, with maximum storm totals of 30 to 40 inches over 
the windward Big Island. Across the remainder of the island chain an 
additional 2 to 4 inches of rainfall is expected, with isolated 
additional totals around 6 inches. This rainfall may produce 
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Lala,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp2.shtml?rainqpf
 
For a list of rainfall observations and wind reports associated with
Lala, see the companion storm summary at WBCSCCNS2 with the WMO
header ACUS42 KWBC or at the following link:
www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/discussions/nfdscc2.html.

STORM SURGE: Water levels may remain elevated through the next tide 
cycle due to persistent large and dangerous wave activity.
 
SURF: Large waves generated by Lala will continue to impact exposed 
waters of the Hawaiian Islands through tonight, with a gradual 
downward trend expected from east to west by Monday. 
Life-threatening surf and rip current conditions will continue. 
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sun Aug 16 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 162055
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  18
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sun Aug 16 2026

The satellite presentation of Lala is highlighted by a large, curved 
convective band that extends over the northern and eastern sides of 
the storm. A small area of central convection obscures the low-level 
center, and a large dry slot wraps around the southern and eastern 
portions of the circulation. Objective and subjective satellite 
intensity estimates have continued to decrease this morning, and the 
initial intensity is set at 55 kt, in best agreement with recent 
D-MINT and D-PRINT estimates from UW-CIMSS.

After moving northwestward for much of the morning, recent radar 
fixes indicate Lala has sped up and begun its westward turn. A 
subtropical ridge over the central Pacific should keep Lala moving 
westward during the next couple of days. The track forecast for days 
3-5 remains challenging. There is slightly better agreement among 
the track guidance this cycle on the storm turning northwestward 
later in the period as an upper-level trough induces a weakness in 
the subtropical ridge. However, there is still a bifurcation of GFS 
and Google Deep Mind ensemble solutions, with some members 
continuing westward across the International Date Line. With the 
overall track envelope shifting eastward this cycle, the updated NHC 
track forecast lies to the right of the previous one at most 
forecast times. This adjustment is in the direction of the latest 
multi-model consensus aids and the Google Deep Mind ensemble mean.

Given Lala's disorganized structure, its proximity to the Hawaiian 
Islands, and the drier environment surrounding the storm, little 
change in strength is expected during the next 24 h. Once Lala pulls 
away from Hawaii, warm SSTs along the forecast track could allow for 
some reintensification. However, moderate west-northwesterly shear 
and continued dry air in the environment could temper the amount 
of strengthening that occurs. The NHC intensity forecast has been 
nudged upward in the 36-72 h period and shows Lala becoming a 
hurricane again by midweek. The forecast still lies below the 
intensity consensus (IVCN), which is higher due to the stronger 
hurricane regional model solutions.  
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Tropical-storm-force winds, accompanied by gusts to near 
hurricane strength, will persist over Maui County, Oahu, and Kauai 
County today. The strongest winds will occur over areas of higher 
terrain. 
 
2. Rain will continue to taper off across the Big Island and Maui 
this afternoon, however additional areas of flash flooding and 
mudslides will be possible. Otherwise, heavy rainfall and the 
potential for flooding and mudslides from Lala will continue across 
the rest of the island chain through later tonight. 
 
3. Large and dangerous waves are expected to persist across portions 
of the Hawaiian Islands today. Surf is building along east-facing 
shores and will increase along exposed southern shores as Lala 
passes through the region. This heavy surf may cause localized
coastal flooding and significant beach erosion.
 
4. Use caution after Lala passes as deadly hazards remain, including 
flooded areas and downed power lines. If you use a generator, be 
sure it is placed outside at least 20 feet away from doors, windows, 
and garages to avoid deadly carbon monoxide poisoning.
